  C14 Workflow SHA-pin integrity. Every third-party GitHub Actions `uses:`
      ref in .github/workflows/ MUST be pinned to a full 40-hex commit
      SHA, not a mutable tag or branch (local ./ and ../ action paths are
      exempt). Mechanizes the SHA-pinning rule of

      primitive, which fails a vanished or empty workflow directory so the
      check cannot go vacuous. Default-mode only: .github/ is
      framework-envelope, never part of a bootstrap-injected consumer
      payload. (Feature 058.)

  C15 Capability-profile <-> AGF-role correspondence. Each of the five
      capability profiles (standard/capability_profiles.md) maps to a role
      defined in standard/AGF.md, and C15 enforces that mapping through
      BOTH vetted primitives from tools/verify_lib.sh:
      vlib_profiles_cover_roles guards the 5<->5 coverage (a dropped
      profile or role fails C15), and vlib_profiles_map_roles parses each
      profile row's explicit Role column, failing unless every row names
      its own role -- a swapped profile-to-role mapping fails C15.
      Default-mode only: a framework-authoring invariant the consumer
      inherits already-verified. (Feature 058 mechanized the coverage;
      phase-014 feature 109, NDEBT-026, added the Role column and the
      mapping primitive.)

      not flag a pre-contract-first complete feature with no contract

      Default-mode only: --payload passes trivially by design (.agent/
      governance state is never part of the bootstrap.sh payload), and a
      --target feature-list-shaped file gets schema-only validation.

design_notes.serialization: Do not run tools/validate.sh and tools/fixtures_self_test.sh at the same time, in this tree or in one scratch copy. Captures are serial and foreground. AT1 and AT5 run the full default sweep; AT6 runs the --payload sweep; AT7 runs the fixture self-test; S04 runs the sweep once more; S05 runs five scratch cases one at a time, each of which runs validate.sh (some twice, default then --payload, inside one bash -c). Never overlap any of these with the fixture self-test, and never take a scratch copy while either script is running in the source tree. scratch_run copies the tree, including the untracked .nizam/ if present; that is harmless for these cases because C9 exempts .nizam/ and no case asserts anything about it.
hazards: 1. The untracked .nizam/ directory (238 files, stale v1.4.0 dogfood payload) in the shared tree is not part of this feature. S03 refuses to run in a tree where .nizam/ is untracked; the attempt worktree (git worktree add from <B>) does not contain it. Never add it to scope, never count it in any evidence, and never assert anything about it.

2. AT1 is existence-only: its paragraph regex is '^  '+i+r'\s+\S', so a one-line stub '  C14 x' would satisfy it. S05 case 1 pins this reality (a corrupted C15 paragraph still passes AT1's coverage), and S04 pins the full paragraph strings byte-for-byte. The content burden is on S04, not on AT1; do not 'fix' AT1 and do not add content assertions to the feature list.

3. AT2's split anchors are the literal '  C5 ' and '  C6 ' and AT3's is 'Payload-doc set'. The pinned C5 paragraph keeps its header and trailing blank line; the pinned insert block contains no '  C5 '/'  C6 ' substring; the Payload-doc set paragraph keeps its exact opening line and gains no earlier 'Payload-doc set' occurrence. S04 re-runs both slicings on the pinned result.

4. Do not edit the --payload option paragraph (lines 128-158 at <A>, NDEBT-045). It still says methodology/ and ecosystem/ are non-injected and lists 'C1-C5, C7-C11'; that drift is deliberately out of scope. The first unchanged_regions pin covers it.

5. Do not touch check_c15_capability_profile_roles' call semantics; 109 owns the dual-primitive call. 108's C15 paragraph only documents it, and both primitive names are pinned in the text. standard/capability_profiles.md, standard/AGF.md, and tools/verify_lib.sh stay byte-identical.

6. The C5 correction is text-only. Do NOT add -i to the grep or otherwise change the sweep: capitalised brand prose must keep passing, and AT2 proves the text matches the code as-is. A 'drive-by' behavior change would also break the frozen AT5 baseline comparison.

7. interface.md is consumer-shipped. The correction is a PATCH under NDS Section 4 (a correction that does not change the document's meaning): 0.3.0 -> 0.3.1 with one change_log entry. Do not skip the version bump (C8 fails a version change with no change record) and do not renumber Section 5 (AT-adjacent S04 asserts exactly 10 items; the feature list's PATCH classification depends on it).
8. Evidence files: line 1 is the invocation, the body is raw output, the last line is EXIT:<code> from the process. No '| tee' and no '| grep' on a capture. A later edit invalidates the captures.
9. C16's --payload banner line is long but still matches AT1's '^\[(C\d+)\]' id extraction; no AT1-relevant output shape changes, because no check code changes.
10. The shared tree's run_state differs from main's by the Orchestrator's feature-108 start entry; S02/S03 allowlist it and reject any further Generator edit. Do not edit run_state to 'clean up'.

failure_triage.DEFECT: An acceptance or S failure caused by the Generator's files. Repair inside the attempt budget: attempt 1 direct fix, attempt 2 type or interface analysis, attempt 3 architectural review. Attempt 4 is forbidden.
failure_triage.CONTRACT_DEFECT: A pin or an S check that a correct implementation cannot satisfy -- for example the premise probe failing on the pinned edits, a pinned string not occurring exactly once at <A>, or an unchanged_file that the edits genuinely require changing (e.g. a README row found stale). Halt, report, and propose a revision of this contract. Do not edit an acceptance test. Do not edit the --payload option paragraph, the C15 call, or the C5 grep to force a pass.
failure_triage.ENVIRONMENT: A missing interpreter, a changed jsonschema version, a TMPDIR inside the repository, or a failure to create the attempt worktree. Halt and escalate. Do not consume an attempt.
